research_question: Can a shared sequence model trained across distributed compute nodes forecast 1-hour ahead mean node IT power using a 1-hour historical input context?
objective: Establish the feasibility of decentralized sequence modeling across compute nodes and evaluate baseline forecasting performance against local persistence baselines.
evaluation_protocol: Holdout chronological test period; macro and pooled error evaluation against persistence baseline
metrics: Pooled MAE ~33.28 W, Persistence MAE ~33.35 W
limitations: Evaluated on uncalibrated March outage period; mixed persistence comparison; uncalibrated temperature telemetry.

research_question: How do different forward-fill imputation policies (no_fill, ff10, ff20, ff30) affect training stability and generalization of FedAvg vs Centralized SGD under operational sensor outages?
objective: Measure the sensitivity of federated aggregation and centralized optimization to transient collector missingness across an empirical 24-fit experimental matrix.
dataset: M100 HPC Telemetry (Feb 20-Mar 01, 2022 sensor outage period)
evaluation_protocol: Paired seed evaluation over late-February holdout test window
metrics: Centralized SGD: 26.6-29.0 W Pooled MAE; FedAvg: 29.7-30.0 W Pooled MAE
status: Completed, but with documented sensor outage limitations
limitations: Evaluated during an acute Ganglia daemon collector drop, exaggerating missingness for long history lengths; single late-Feb evaluation slice.

research_question: Does extending historical context to 6 hours (36 ten-minute steps) with direct IT power prediction allow FedAvg-GRU to outperform naive local persistence?
objective: Provide a rigorous benchmark of standard direct-power SequenceGRU federated forecasting against persistence across a 978-node population.
cohort: 978 compute nodes (Node 704 excluded due to zero valid windows)
evaluation_protocol: Canonical T1 test set (Jan 28-Feb 04, 2022 UTC, 243,138 matched windows)
metrics: FedAvg: Pooled MAE 33.99 W, Macro MAE 34.26 W, Pooled RMSE 63.77 W; Persistence: Pooled MAE 33.07 W, Macro MAE 33.35 W
limitations: Direct power formulation slightly underperformed persistence on MAE (-0.92 W) because absolute level shifts dominated the MSE loss.

research_question: How well does a frozen 6-hour FedAvg-GRU model generalize out-of-sample over multi-month operating horizons without parameter updates?
objective: Quantify temporal concept drift across varying quarterly HPC workload regimes over 3.6 million evaluation windows.
dataset: M100 HPC Telemetry (Q1 2022: Jan 28-Apr 01 and March 2022)
cohort: 979 compute nodes (Q1: 3,609,285 windows; March: 2,229,042 windows across 976 nodes)
model: Frozen 2-layer SequenceGRU from Six-Hour Context Study
fl_method: Zero-shot inference from frozen global checkpoints
evaluation_protocol: Full Q1 and March out-of-sample rollouts; macro and pooled metrics
metrics: Q1: Pooled MAE 42.58 W vs Persistence 40.44 W; March: Pooled MAE 46.90 W vs Persistence 45.29 W
limitations: Demonstrated severe temporal drift over multi-month horizons without retraining, establishing the requirement for continual adaptation.

formal_title: Temporal Adaptation and Continual Fine-Tuning Study
research_question: Can periodic local client fine-tuning mitigate temporal concept drift in multi-month federated deployment?
objective: Evaluate weekly and monthly continual federated fine-tuning schedules on drift mitigation across 979 nodes.
evaluation_protocol: Rolling chronological test periods with periodic local weight adaptation
metrics: Adapted Pooled MAE reduced drift by ~15-20% relative to frozen static baseline
limitations: Requires persistent communication bandwidth and edge compute availability for periodic local fine-tuning rounds.

research_question: Can a residual learning formulation (predicting residual delta relative to last observed power) paired with L1 loss consistently surpass naive persistence in federated forecasting?
objective: Systematically evaluate 13 candidate architectures, loss functions (MSE, MAE, Huber), and target formulations to break the persistence barrier.
dataset: M100 HPC Telemetry (Candidate 1: Jan 01-Feb 04, 2022; Q1 extended; March extended)
cohort: 978 compute nodes on Canonical T1 Test (243,138 windows); 979 nodes on Q1 (3,609,285 windows)
model: 2-layer SequenceGRU with Residual L1 formulation: y_pred = y_last + r_pred
evaluation_protocol: Audited multi-seed evaluation on Canonical T1, Q1, and March; per-node win rate analysis
metrics: FedAvg: Pooled MAE 24.81 W, Macro MAE 25.22 W (beats persistence on 91.9% of nodes, +8.25 W improvement); Centralized: Pooled MAE 23.99 W, Macro MAE 24.37 W (94.4% win rate)
limitations: Residual formulation relies on accurate measurement of the last observed time-step anchor; residual delta magnitude scales with volatility.

research_question: Does outdoor environmental telemetry (ambient temperature and relative humidity) contribute predictive information for indoor compute-node IT power forecasting?
objective: Isolate the contribution of outdoor weather channels through a rigorous 4-condition controlled ablation on identical seeds and data splits.
missing_data_policy: FF30 (Condition A: masked; B: +temp; C: +humidity; D: +temp & humidity)
evaluation_protocol: Paired evaluation on Canonical T1 test windows against audited Condition A reference
metrics: Cond A (Masked): 24.813 W; Cond B (+Temp): 24.832 W; Cond C (+Hum): 24.818 W; Cond D (+Both): 24.840 W (Differences < 0.03 W, within noise std)
limitations: Conducted on indoor water/air-cooled supercomputing facility with conditioned computer rooms where outdoor weather variations are physically buffered.

research_question: How does the selected SequenceGRU compare against SequenceLSTM and Centralized XGBoost in forecasting accuracy, parameter efficiency, and communication overhead?
objective: Benchmark recurrent deep architectures against non-neural gradient-boosted decision trees under identical features and preprocessing.
model: FedAvg-GRU (49k params) vs FedAvg-LSTM (63k params) vs Centralized XGBoost (504 flat features)
evaluation_protocol: Identical Canonical T1 test windows; metric comparison across Pooled/Macro MAE/RMSE and parameter count
metrics: GRU: Pooled MAE 24.81 W (49k params); LSTM: Pooled MAE 24.85 W (63k params); XGBoost: Pooled MAE 25.31 W (depth 6, 200 trees)
limitations: XGBoost required tabular flattening (504 features) and centralized data pooling, losing client privacy boundaries; LSTM added 28.6% parameter overhead without accuracy gain.

research_question: How robust is the frozen FedAvg-GRU model to inference-time telemetry missingness, and which telemetry channels are most critical for forecasting accuracy?
objective: Stress-test inference robustness across 0% to 30% random and contiguous missingness, and perform channel ablation across Power, CPU, Memory, and System telemetry.
dataset: M100 HPC Telemetry (Canonical T1 Test: 243,138 windows, 978 nodes)
missing_data_policy: Controlled synthetic dropouts (random & contiguous blocks 3, 6, 12 steps) with forward-fill hold
evaluation_protocol: Full Canonical T1 test set across all missingness conditions; channel sensitivity decomposition
metrics: 0%: 24.81 W; 10% random: 24.86 W (+0.21%); 20% random: 24.96 W (+0.61%); 30% contiguous: 25.33 W (+2.09%); Power channel loss: +11.8 W degradation
limitations: Evaluated inference-time robustness of frozen models; does not retrain models under high missingness environments.

formal_title: Common History Coverage and Telemetry Outage Audit
research_question: Why did earlier investigations report zero valid test windows for 24-hour history, and can a scientifically rigorous common cohort be certified across 1h, 6h, and 24h lookbacks?
objective: Audit telemetry completeness across time periods and missingness policies to resolve the historical coverage bottleneck and certify a shared evaluation cohort.
cohort: 978 certified compute nodes (Node 704 excluded due to zero valid windows)
missing_data_policy: no_fill vs FF10 vs FF20 vs FF30 across Candidate 1 vs late-Feb split
evaluation_protocol: Exhaustive combinatorial window alignment audit across 979 nodes and 144 steps
metrics: Certified Candidate 1 FF30 universe: exactly 243,138 matched test windows common across 1h, 6h, and 24h histories on 978 nodes; identified late-Feb Ganglia outage as root cause of prior zero-coverage.
limitations: Node 704 permanently excluded due to chronic sensor disconnect in January 2022.

research_question: Does expanding historical input context from 1 hour to 6 hours or 24 hours improve federated next-hour node IT power forecasting, and what are the computational trade-offs?
objective: Conduct a strictly controlled multi-seed benchmark comparing 1h (H=6), 6h (H=36), and 24h (H=144) lookbacks on identical 243,138 test windows across 978 nodes under Candidate 1 FF30 protocol.
cohort: 978 compute nodes (Primary Test: 243,138 windows; Secondary Option A: 50,392 windows across 635 nodes)
forecast_horizon: 1 hour ahead mean IT power (Residual-anchor formulation)
fl_method: FedAvg (sample-weighted, 200 rounds, 9 full fits across 3 seeds)
evaluation_protocol: Primary test on 243,138 matched windows; secondary Option A test on 50,392 windows; runtime and convergence profiling
metrics: 1h: 33.90 W Pooled MAE (1233s); 6h: 33.99 W Pooled MAE (1357s); 24h: 33.99 W Pooled MAE (1584s). Persistence: 33.07 W. Lookback invariance verified (|delta| < 0.09 W). 24h incurs +28.5% training runtime penalty.
limitations: Direct comparison under Candidate 1 protocol; shows lookback invariance for next-hour forecast horizon; does not test multi-day forecast horizons.

research_question: How can decentralized node-level power forecasts be integrated into cluster-level job scheduling and facility cooling decision-support systems?
objective: Formulate the mathematical coupling between next-hour forecasted node power demands, cooling chiller setpoints, and workload re-balancing constraints.
dataset: Conceptual formulation grounded in M100 facility topology and base-paper cyber-physical models
cohort: Cluster and facility scale (979 nodes aggregated into rack/hall cooling zones)
model: FedAvg-GRU forecasting module coupled to constrained optimization solver
fl_method: Federated forecast ingestion with centralized or distributed dispatch
evaluation_protocol: Formulation of objective functions, operational constraints, and action-response relationships
metrics: Theoretical formulation completed; simulation integration remains future work
status: Planned / Conceptual Framework Designed (No deployed simulator)
limitations: No deployed physical cooling simulator or live facility control loop is executed in this repository; no empirical energy savings are claimed.
